texts.preamble: Balaji Trading Company Through Its ... vs Skb Traders Through Its Proprietor Shri ... on 4 September, 2025 Cs (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s Skb Traders: Dod: 04.09. In The Court Of Vinod Yadav: District Judge (Commercial Court)-02: North-West District: Rohini Courts: New Delhi Cnr No.DLNW01-011923-2024 Civil Suit (Comm.) No.774/2024
texts.facts: As per the case set up by the plaintiff, the defendant was supplied various goods by it under invoice(s) and a running account in respect thereof was being maintained, which showed outstanding amount of Rs.3,65,582/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Sixty Five Thousand Five Hundred Balaji Trading Company Through Its ... vs Skb Traders Through Its Proprietor Shri ... on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76129814/ 1 Eighty Two Only) as on 06.07.2022. The defendant did not make payment of the outstanding amount. The plaintiff accordingly sent legal notice on 16.09.2024, the tracking report whereof suggests that the same was duly served upon the defendant. No reply thereto was furnished by the defendant. 3. Therefore, the plaintiff has filed the instant suit against the defendant, inter alia seeking a decree in the sum of Rs.3,65,582/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Sixty Five Thousand Five Hundred Eighty Two Only) alongwith interest @ 18% per annum w.e.f 06.07.2022 till realization thereof. 4. It is pertinent to mention here that prior to filing the present suit, plaintiff had also exhausted the remedy of pre-institution mediation in terms of Section 12-A of Commercial Courts Act, 2015. The defendant refused to participate in the pre-institution mediation. Accordingly, Certificate of Non-Starter Report dated 22.11.2024 was issued in the matter. 5. After getting served with the summons, defendant filed written statement, inter alia denying the receipt of goods in one breath and CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 questioning the quality of goods in another breath. The reference was made to FIR No.585/2022, U/s 420/272/273/120-B IPC, PS Mangolpuri, lodged by one Shri Jitender Singh against the plaintiff, wherein there were allegations of supply of spurious and sub-standard quality of kiryana goods by the plaintiff to his that customer. The defendant has questioned the entitlement of plaintiff to recover the suit amount from it on the basis of aforesaid FIR. 6. Plaintiff filed replication, inter alia denying the averments made in the written statement and reiterating the ones made in the plaint. 8. Pursuant to framing of issues, vide order dated 09.07.2025 itself, Ms.Rabiya, Advocate was appointed as "Local Commissioner" to record evidence in the matter. 9. (a) In order to discharge the onus of proving issues put upon it, plaintiff firm examined its Authorized Representative Shri Anshul Bansal CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 as PW-1 in the matter, who in his evidence by Balaji Trading Company Through Its ... vs Skb Traders Through Its Proprietor Shri ... on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76129814/ 2 way of Affidavit Ex.PW1/A has reiterated the averments made in the plaint and referred to the following documents: (i) Duly attested copy of Registration Certificate [Form GST REG-06] in respect of the plaintiff firm namely M/s Balaji Trading Co., as Ex.PW1/1; (ii) True copy of Authority Letter dated 19.04.2024, executed by plaintiff firm in favour of PW-1 as Ex.PW1/2 (OSR); (iii) True copy of the ledger account maintained by the plaintiff firm in respect of the transactions done with the defendant for the period from 01.04.2022 to 31.03.2023, wherein a sum of Rs.3,65,482/- is being shown as "Debit Balance" as on 06.07.2022 as Ex.PW1/3; (iv) True copy(ies) of Invoice bearing No.8, dated 01.04.2022, for Rs.10,001/-; Invoice No.49, dated 02.04.2022, for a sum of Rs.32,200/-; Invoice No.50, dated 02.04.2022, for a sum of Rs.15,880/-; Invoice No.119, dated 03.04.2022, for a sum of Rs.91,501/-; Invoice No.141, dated 05.04.2022, for a sum of Rs.12,900/-; Invoice No.457, dated 26.04.2022, for a sum of Rs.41,000/-; Invoice No.644, dated 05.05.2022, for a sum of Rs.81,000/-; Invoice No.1042, dated 21.05.2022, for a sum of Rs.32,400/-; and Invoice No.1104, dated 25.05.2022, for a sum of Rs.48,600/- as Ex.PW1/4 (Colly); (v) True copy of legal notice dated 16.09.2024, sent on behalf of plaintiff to the defendant as Ex.PW1/5; CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 (vi) Original Tracking Receipt and Internet downloaded tracking report as Ex.PW1/6; (vii) Certificate of Non-Starter Report dated 22.11.2024, issued under the signatures of Secretary, DLSA, North-West as Ex.PW1/7; (viii) True copy of order, passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, thereby quashing FIR No.585/2022, U/s 420/272/273/120-B IPC, PS Mangolpuri as Mark A; (ix) True copy of order dated 11.12.2023, passed by Patiala House Court as Mark B; (x) Certificate under Section 63 of Bharatiya Sakshaya Adhiniyam, 2023, issued under the signatures of PW-1 as Ex.PW1/10; (b) PW-1/Shri Anshul Bansal was thoroughly cross In his cross-examination, copy of FIR No.585/2022, U/s 420/272/273/120-B IPC, PS Mangolpuri was put to him as Ex.PW1/D1; and copy of Invoice No.141, dated 05.04.2022, for a sum of Balaji Trading Company Through Its ... vs Skb Traders Through Its Proprietor Shri ... on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76129814/ 3 Rs.12,900/- as Ex.PW1/D2. 10.
texts.arguments: (a) On the other hand, defendant firm examined its Authorized Representative (A.R) Shri Rajender Kumar Gupta as DW-1, who in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.DW1/A has reiterated the averments made in the written statement and referred to the following documents: (i) Original Special Power of Attorney, dated 25.02.2025, executed by defendant firm in favour of DW-1 as Ex.DW1/1; CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 (ii) Copy of Aadhar Card of DW-1 as Ex.DW1/2 (OSR); (iii) Colour photographs of the products supplied by plaintiff to the defendant as Ex.DW1/3 (Colly); (vi) Video-CD of the products supplied by plaintiff to the defendant as Ex.DW1/4; (v) Affidavit under Section 63 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 as Ex.DW1/5; (v) Copy of complaint dated 30.05.2022 as Ex.DW1/6; (vi) Copy of Notice under Section 41 Cr.P.C, dated 30.05.2022 as Mark A; (vii) Copy of FIR No.585/2022, U/s 420./272/273/120-B IPC, PS Mangolpuri was proved as already Ex.PW1/D1; (b) DW-1/Shri Rajender Kumar Gupta was thoroughly cross- examined by learned counsel for the plaintiff. (c) Defendant further examined Shri Puneet Kumar, S/o Shri Vinod Kumar as DW-2, who in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.DW2/A stated that he was the proprietor of M/s Puneet Retails and plaintiff firm had supplied fake, duplicate and sub-standard/inferior quality of goods/food products to him for which he got lodged FIR No.585/2022, dated 24.06.2022, U/s 420./272/273/120-B IPC with PS Mangolpuri. This witness further stated that proceedings under Section 3/26/51/59 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 2006 has been pending against the plaintiff in the Court of learned ACJM, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi. CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 The learned counsel for the plaintiff has very vehemently argued that the goods were supplied to the defendant through Invoices Ex.PW1/4 (Colly) on various dates; the ledger account in respect thereof has been duly proved on record as Ex.PW1/3. It is next contended that the defendant never questioned either the receipt of goods or quality thereof at any stage, except for a complaint dated 30.05.2022 Ex.DW1/6, wherein defendant categorically admitted receipt of the goods, however, questioned the quality of goods on the premise that an FIR had been registered by the police against the plaintiff for supplying spurious material to some other person. It was nowhere mentioned in the said complaint that the material supplied by the plaintiff to the defendant was not received. Even there has CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 not been mention of any customer of the defendant having pointed out the defect in the goods sold by it to them. 14. It is next contended that the legal notice Ex.PW1/5 was correctly addressed to the defendant and despite presumption of the service thereof, the defendant did not file any reply thereto and as such, the defendant did not have any defence to deny outstanding payment to the plaintiff. 15. Per contra, learned counsel for the defendant has very vehemently argued that PW-1/Shri Anshul Bansal has no authority to depose on behalf of plaintiff as the SPA Ex.PW1/2 does not bear acknowledgment or acceptance by him. It is next contended that the defendant did not receive the material mentioned in invoices as the invoices neither bear the signatures nor stamp of plaintiff nor that of defendant. It is next contended that the ledger account filed by the plaintiff cannot be believed to be correct, as it is not accompanied by any duly audited balance-sheet showing the name of defendant in the list of creditors. The learned counsel has termed the invoices Ex.PW1/4 (Colly) as forged and fabricated. 16. As regards the argument of learned counsel for the defendant that Ex.PW1/2 is not a valid attorney authorizing PW-1 to depose on behalf of plaintiff in the matter for want of signatures of this witness on this document, it is noted that the law does not require the Authorized CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 Representative to have his acknowledgment on the attorney. The requirement of law simply is that an attorney can depose on behalf of plaintiff regarding facts to the extent of his knowledge of the facts which happened in his knowledge. In one breath the defendant has questioned the authority of PW-1 to depose in the matter, but in the same breath the attorney issued by defendant in the name of DW-1 also does not bear his signature towards acknowledgment, making him an Authorized Representative of defendant. , the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has been pleased to lay down as under: xxxxx 8. It was observed by the learned trial court that under the Sales of Goods Act, the presumption is that if there did not exist any defect in the goods, no counter claim has been set up by the defendant claiming damages to supply defects, it cannot be presumed that deductions are made on the ground of infirmities in the goods. Further, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case reported as, "RFA No.479/2006", titled as, "M/s Kumar Industries V/s Suresh Kumar Mittal" (DOD: 10.10.2018) has been pleased to lay down as under: xxxxx 6. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case reported as, "1980 RLR (Note 44)", titled as, "Kalu Ram V/s Sita Ram" has been pleased to hold that adverse presumption will be drawn if the legal notice is not replied to. The relevant portion of the said judgment reads as under: xxxxx "It was held that the plaintiff before filing suit had served defendant with a notice making serious allegations that defendant was a trespasser and that his possession was illegal. xxxxx (Emphasis supplied) (ii) Further, on the same aspect, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case reported as, "98 (2002) DLT 573", titled as, "Metropolis Travels & Resorts (I) Pvt. Ltd. V/s Sumit Kalra & Ors.", (DOD: 07.05.2002) has been pleased to lay down as under: This Court in the case of Kalu Ram v. Sita Ram 1980 RLR (Note) 44 observed that service of notice having been admitted without reservation and that having not been replied in that eventuality adverse inference should be drawn because he kept quite over the notice and did not send any reply. Even on the similar aspect in case reported as, "RFA (OS) No.93/2010", titled as, "Krishan Kumar Aggarwal V/s Life Insurance Corporation" (DOD: 29.08.2014), the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has been pleased to lay down as under: xxxxx 65) No explanation has been rendered by the respondent as to why letter dated 23rd August, 2008 and the legal notice sent by the appellant were not repudiated or even replied. In the judicial precedents reported in Rakesh Kumar Vs. Hindustan Everest Tool Ltd. (1988) 2 SCC 165 & Hiralal Kapur Vs. Prabhu Chaudhary (1988) 2 SCC 172 it was held by the Supreme Court that a categorical assertion by the landlord in a legal notice if not replied to and controverted, can be treated as an admission by a tenant. 66) In a Division Bench proceedings of this court reported in Metropolis Travels & Resorts Vs. Sumit Kalra 98 (2002) DLT 573 (DB), no adverse inference was drawn against the respondent for failure to reply the legal notice on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case. Reference was made to proceedings reported in Kalu Ram Vs. Sita Ram 1980 RLR (note) 44 wherein it had been observed that service of notice being admitted without reservation and that having not been replied, in that eventuality adverse inference should be drawn. xxxxx 24.
